target_schema.title: Unified Synthea and OMOP Healthcare Schema

fields.name: person_source_value

fields.name: death_date
fields.description: Person date of death when known.

fields.name: gender_source_value
fields.description: Gender value as represented by the source.

fields.name: race_source_value

fields.name: ethnicity_source_value

fields.name: marital_status_source_value

fields.name: location_source_value

fields.name: encounter_count

fields.name: visit_description

fields.name: reason_description

fields.name: provider_id

fields.name: start_datetime

fields.name: drug_exposure_id

fields.name: visit_id
fields.description: Visit associated with the drug exposure.

fields.name: exposure_category

fields.name: start_datetime
fields.description: Drug exposure start or administration date and time.

fields.name: end_datetime
fields.description: Drug exposure end date and time.

fields.name: reason_source_code
fields.description: Source code for the prescribing reason.

fields.name: procedure_id
fields.description: Unique procedure identifier; generated for sources without an event key.

fields.name: visit_id
fields.description: Visit during which the procedure occurred.

fields.name: reason_source_code
fields.description: Source code for the procedure reason.

fields.name: observation_kind

fields.name: person_id

fields.name: value_number
fields.description: Numeric result, normalized to the applicable SI unit when the quantity is physical and convertible.

fields.name: unit_concept_id
fields.description: Standardized unit concept, representing the SI unit where applicable.

fields.name: range_low
fields.description: Lower reference limit in the same normalized unit as the result.

fields.name: range_high
fields.description: Upper reference limit in the same normalized unit as the result.

fields.name: visit_id
fields.description: Visit where the plan was initiated.

fields.name: reason_source_code

fields.name: cost_id

fields.name: cost_event_id
fields.description: Identifier of the clinical event to which the cost applies.

fields.name: cost_category
fields.description: Atomic category for source line-item or encounter base cost.

fields.name: source_cost_amount
fields.description: Cost amount supplied by Synthea for the associated source event.

conflicts.description: The same human subject entity is named patients in Synthea and person in OMOP, with differing attribute names such as birthdate versus birth_datetime.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the singular canonical resource person and descriptive snake_case field names while retaining exact source provenance.

conflicts.description: Synthea encounter and OMOP visit occurrence represent the same high-level care interaction under different terminology.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both as visit; OMOP visit detail remains a finer-grained source structure rather than being conflated with the encounter identity.

conflicts.description: Equivalent provider specialty attributes use a misspelling and different naming conventions.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized the target name to specialty_source_value.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea imaging columns contain spaces and violate target naming conventions.
conflicts.resolution: Converted all target identifiers to snake_case without changing their semantics.

conflicts.description: Monetary amounts are mostly declared as strings, despite representing numeric quantities.
conflicts.resolution: Represented monetary amounts as number and retained currency separately through a concept identifier.

conflicts.description: Counts are represented as strings in multiple source structures.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical count attributes use integer.

conflicts.description: Synthea declares the value datatype as number while storing the actual result as string; OMOP separates typed result columns.
conflicts.resolution: Used separate numeric, string, and concept-valued result fields and retained the source datatype declaration independently.

conflicts.description: Fields described as date-times are declared as date in both source schemas.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical event timestamps use datetime, while genuinely date-only attributes remain date.

conflicts.description: Invalidation reason codes are incorrectly typed as date in several OMOP resources.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical invalidation reason attributes use string.

conflicts.description: Textual values are incorrectly declared as integer.
conflicts.resolution: Canonical names and prescription directions use string.

conflicts.description: Coordinates are declared as strings.
conflicts.resolution: Coordinates use number in decimal degrees.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores a SNOMED source code directly, whereas OMOP distinguishes a standardized concept identifier from the verbatim source code.
conflicts.resolution: Kept standardized concept identity and source code in separate fields; no source code was treated as an OMOP concept identifier without vocabulary mapping.

conflicts.description: Units may be free text, source codes, or standardized concepts and may use non-SI scales.
conflicts.resolution: Retained verbatim units separately and defined numeric physical results to be normalized to the applicable SI unit, with the standardized unit concept recording the normalized unit.

conflicts.description: Synthea uses compact M/F encoding while OMOP distinguishes source values from standardized concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved source encoding in gender_source_value and kept the standardized concept in a distinct foreign key.

conflicts.description: The Synthea encounter field named provider semantically references an organization, while OMOP provider_id references a clinician.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped the Synthea field only to care_site_id and kept clinician provider_id semantically separate.

conflicts.description: Medication codes use RxNorm, immunization codes use CVX, and OMOP drug source values can use multiple vocabularies.
conflicts.resolution: Unified them as drug exposures but retained the source code and an explicit exposure category; standardized concept assignment remains vocabulary-aware.

conflicts.description: Synthea cost is a base or line-item amount, while OMOP distinguishes charged, incurred, and paid amounts.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved Synthea amounts as source_cost_amount and kept OMOP financial measures separate rather than asserting false equivalence.

conflicts.description: Synthea repeats address attributes inside person, organization, and provider tables, while OMOP normalizes addresses into location.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted a normalized location resource referenced by people and care sites; provider location can be represented through its care site.

conflicts.description: Multiple identifier types are stored as separate columns on the patient record.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized identifiers into person_identifier with one atomic identifier type and value per row.

conflicts.description: Synthea combines laboratory measurements and observations, while OMOP decomposes them into domain-specific tables.
conflicts.resolution: Created a common clinical_observation resource with an explicit observation_kind discriminator and typed values.

conflicts.description: Synthea separates immunizations from medications, while OMOP can represent administrations in drug exposure.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both event forms in drug_exposure and preserved their category explicitly.

conflicts.description: Synthea embeds costs on clinical event rows, while OMOP stores cost in a separate polymorphic resource.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized all financial values into cost, linked conceptually to the applicable clinical event.

conflicts.description: OMOP supports a two-level visit hierarchy, whereas Synthea provides only a single encounter level.
conflicts.resolution: Used visit as the common encounter level; OMOP visit-detail hierarchy is retained as optional finer-grained information rather than merged into unrelated event identifiers.

conflicts.description: Embedded source addresses imply one address snapshot per entity row, while a normalized location may be shared by many entities.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled many people or care sites to one location through foreign keys and avoided embedding composite addresses.

conflicts.description: The wide Synthea patient row limits each identifier category to at most one value, while identifiers are conceptually repeatable.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled person to person_identifier as one-to-many.

conflicts.description: Synthea has one encounter level, while OMOP permits one visit occurrence to contain many visit details.
conflicts.resolution: Kept the common visit grain and treated detail records as optional children when that OMOP granularity is needed.

conflicts.description: A source observation has one polymorphic result, represented through different physical columns in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Retained mutually exclusive typed value columns on one clinical observation row rather than creating multiple observation rows.

conflicts.description: Several OMOP resources use polymorphic references that can target multiple entity domains and cannot be represented by one ordinary foreign key.
conflicts.resolution: Kept domain/type metadata conceptually separate from event identifiers and did not collapse polymorphic identifiers into person, provider, or visit foreign keys.

conflicts.description: Equivalent person entities use different primary-key names, and Synthea does not formally declare its documented key.
conflicts.resolution: Defined person_id as the required primary key with provenance from both source identifiers.

conflicts.description: Equivalent encounter entities use differently named identifiers and only OMOP formally declares the key.
conflicts.resolution: Defined visit_id as the unified primary key with provenance from both source identifiers.

conflicts.description: Organization and care-site identifiers name the same facility identity differently.
conflicts.resolution: Defined care_site_id as the unified facility key with provenance from both sources.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea event tables have no declared or documented event key, while corresponding OMOP resources have event identifiers that are not consistently declared as primary keys.
conflicts.resolution: Established required target event keys; OMOP identifiers supply provenance where present, and deterministic surrogate values are generated for keyless source rows.

conflicts.description: The name provider is a foreign-key homonym: it points to an organization in Synthea encounters but to a clinician in OMOP visits.
conflicts.resolution: Defined separate care_site_id and provider_id foreign keys and never combined their provenance.

conflicts.description: OMOP polymorphic event identifiers do not reference a single declared resource key.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved domain/type discriminators with polymorphic identifiers and avoided declaring invalid ordinary foreign keys.
